title: I Used the Swim-Lane Reservation Against the Coach Who Laned-Blocked

parts.text: I reserved lane 2 at 6:00 a.m. and the coach had cones across 2 and 3 for a private. The reservation board he demanded said: ONE LANE PER BOOKING. NO CONE BLOCKS. I was forty, lap swimmer, holding a QR that said lane 2. Coach Vic said, "Sets need width." I pointed at the board. He tossed another cone. "Width is coaching." I photographed the cones, the board, and my QR. Then I used the pool app to check in, which pings the front desk when a reserved lane is occupied by staff. At 6:05 the desk asked why Vic's name was on a lane-block ticket.
parts.cliffhanger_hint: The desk can see cones on lane 2 against the one-lane board Vic demanded.

social.video_title: The coach coned off my reserved lap lane — Part 1/2
social.description: 6:00 QR, two lanes of cones, and a board he demanded. The app pinged the desk. Would you have split a lane with a set?

parts.text: Vic called it safety until the app showed a private lesson on a public reservation. I printed the ticket, the board, and the photo. Lane 2 opened. Vic coached in 3 and told the deck the board was always about optics. Optics is a word coaches use when an app exists. Lane policy now has a second line: WIDTH BOOKS A SECOND LANE. I lap. Vic pays for 3. The water finally has a rope that matches the QR.

social.video_title: Width books a second lane — Part 2/2
social.description: Lane-block ticket, cones gone, and a second line on the board. Was safety ever two public lanes?
